messages:
elaine: quick check — trying to finalize v3 generate endpoint error semantics before I merge the PR. main questions:
- do we keep returning 400 for client validation (missing fields / wrong types) or switch to 422 for schema errors?
- what's our guidance for retryability: 429 should be retryable with backoff, 503 retryable, but what about partial KVCACHE misses / upstream timeouts (should they map to 502/504)?
- also pinging @tom for any backward-compat constraints on the old sdk.

raj: my quick take — keep 400 for basic request shape problems (missing body, invalid JSON). Use 422 only when the payload is syntactically valid but semantically invalid (e.g., model param incompatible). But we should be conservative: many clients treat 4xx as non-retryable.

tom: +1 to raj's phrasing. important: clients that auto-retry on 400 are common, so moving previously-400 responses to 422 could break existing logic. if we add 422, document it clearly in the migration guide.

maya: for retryability rules I suggested a simple mapping in the PR description: 429 -> retry with jitter/backoff (client quota), 503 -> retry, 502/504 -> retry but escalate if repeated. transient internal errors (timeouts talking to model host) should be surfaced as 502 with a hint field so we can roll them to non-retry later if needed.

elaine: here's an example response shape I'm proposing for validation errors (keeps 400):
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "validation_failed",
  "message": "2 validation errors",
  "validation_errors": [
    {"field": "input.length", "code": "too_long", "message": "input exceeds 64k tokens"},
    {"field": "model", "code": "unsupported", "message": "model 'redwood-alpha' not allowed for this key"}
  ],
  "request_id": "req_abc123"
}
```
This keeps the shape stable for SDKs reading `validation_errors`. Thoughts?

raj: that shape looks good. small nit: add `retryable": false` at top-level error for clients that check one flag. otherwise some client libs end up inspecting codes.

tom: i'd rather avoid `retryable` on all 4xx types. maybe include `retryable_hint` (enum: "always","sometimes","never")? But that complicates server logic. if we add a boolean it should be consistent across all errors.

maya: runtime ops perspective: we already emit structured logs with an internal `transient` tag for 502/503. exposing a `retryable` flag helps debugging, but if we can't guarantee accuracy, clients will misuse it. pref: boolean but conservative: only set true for 429/503/504 and false for 4xx/401/403.

elaine: ok practical compromise: we'll add an optional `retryable` boolean in the error envelope. server will set it for errors we know are transient (429/503/504/timeout). validation 4xx will explicitly set `retryable: false`. documented in the api-contract.md.

tom: fine, as long as docs call out guarantee: "false => do not retry; true => retry with exponential backoff (with jitter)" and that absence of the field means "unknown".

maya: ops note — please ensure observability tags map to this, so we can roll out a monitoring alert for high `retryable:true` rates.

elaine: PR is open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3456 PTAL @tom @raj. i'll update the migration guide and add a short snippet for the SDKs showing how to handle `validation_errors` array and `retryable`.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary: build-2026.3.1 -> canary-us-west (ETA ~5m).

raj: one more edge: streaming endpoints — we currently stream partial tokens and then send an error frame. do we keep the same error envelope shape for final error frame? we should.

elaine: yes keep identical envelope for final error frame (so SDKs can parse it uniformly). i'll add a test case for streaming error frames.

tom: acked. i'll review the PR tonight. if no blockers i'll approve tomorrow morning. :+1:
